title: Severe Nor'easter Breathes Havoc Across East Coast: 1 Dead, Thousands Powerless Amid Raging Floods
snippet: A relentless autumn nor'easter brought dangerously high winds, severe coastal flooding, and widespread power outages to the U.S. Northeast, leaving one dead in New York and forcing event cancellations across the region.
content:
A ferocious, slow-moving nor'easter lashed the U.S. East Coast on Saturday, knocking out electricity to roughly 100,000 homes, turning coastal streets into rivers, and claiming at least one life in New York City.

The sprawling storm system generated wind gusts exceeding 70 mph in some coastal zones and dumped heavy rain from the Mid-Atlantic through New England. In Brooklyn, 56-year-old Leighton Brown, a New York City Housing Authority employee, was tragically struck and killed by a falling tree, marking the storm's first confirmed fatality.

Widespread Inundation and Rescues

Coastal communities bore the brunt of the storm's surge. In Egg Harbor Township, New Jersey, emergency responders pulled nine adults and a dog to safety from flooded motel rooms. Further down the Jersey Shore in Surf City, water spilled into local marinas, damaging high-end watercraft and echoing the destructive surge of historic storms.

Residents on Long Island resorted to paddling kayaks through submerged neighborhood streets, while heavy surf tore away dune fencing in Ocean City, Maryland. In Norfolk, Virginia, persistent tidal flooding left stranded cars lining flooded thoroughfares.

National Weather Service meteorologists cautioned that early-autumn timing amplifies the storm's danger. With trees still full of leaves, wind resistance is significantly higher, dramatically increasing the risk of fallen branches, power line damage, and blocked roadways on rain-soaked soil.

Major Disruption to Travel and Events

The system severely disrupted weekend plans across the Eastern Seaboard. FlightAware recorded hundreds of flight cancellations at Boston Logan International Airport, alongside massive grounding of regional flights to Martha's Vineyard and Nantucket. Ferries along the barrier islands were similarly halted.

Major events took a heavy blow as well. Major League Baseball was forced to alter the final regular-season series between the Boston Red Sox and Chicago Cubs, shifting their final game to St. Petersburg, Florida. High-profile cancellations included Ed Sheeran’s sold-out stadium shows in Foxborough, Massachusetts, New York City’s Global Citizen Festival, and the Oceans Calling music festival in Maryland.

Forecasters expect the rapidly intensifying storm to linger near the New Jersey coastline through Monday before finally moving out by Tuesday, prolonging high tides, heavy rains, and damaging winds for tens of millions of residents.
